plan.major: English and Writing Studies: Professional Writing Concentration
plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-14 from the official Salem College 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (current edition, catoid=34), English and Writing Studies Major (BA) program page (poid=901), Professional Writing concentration. Salem College publishes major requirements but no official semester sequence for this program (its Print Degree Planner is a blank worksheet), so the plan is collected in requirements_only form as a single block. The recorded total is the major requirement only; the full degree requirements, including the Salem Impact core (published separately in the same catalog), are not itemized here. Per-course credits are the Hour(s) values printed on each course's own official course detail page in the same catalog; the program page itself prints no per-course credits. Prerequisites naming courses outside this plan are disclosed in these notes and are not recorded as plan prerequisites. The catalog states the major requires ten courses (minimum of 30 semester hours): three core courses plus seven courses in a concentration (minimum 21 semester hours), and that to be used toward the major each course must be taken for 3 or 4 semester hours. Residency as printed (re-verified live 2026-11-14): at least six of the 10 required courses, including ENGL 380, must be completed at Salem. The core's ENGL 214 is the cross-listed ENGL 214 / HHMN 214 course, counted once. Catalog typos transcribed as printed in titles: ENGL 365 'Natative' [sic]; ENGL 250's GenEd line prints 'Service Learnng' [sic]. Concentration notes as printed: a maximum of three semester hours of internship (ENGL 270) can be used as an elective toward the concentration, and typically a maximum of two independent or two honors independent studies can be used as electives, each taken for a minimum of 3 semester hours; exceptions require the program director's approval. The Theory/Rhetoric/Composition choose-one options ENGL 255 and HHMN 255 are a cross-listed pair (HHMN 255's detail states the cross-listing; ENGL 255's own detail does not), listed as printed. The recorded total (30) is core 9 + concentration 21, the catalog's printed minimum.

courses.title: Literary Theory, Rhetoric and Composition Elective
courses.choice_note: Choose one course for the Literary Theory, Rhetoric and Composition block. All seven catalog options are printed at 3 Hour(s) with no prerequisites. ENGL 255 / HHMN 255 are a cross-listed pair (see plan notes).

options.title: The Rhetoric of Health and Medicine

courses.title: Literature in English
courses.choice_note: Choose four courses in total for the Literature in English block (this is one of the four choice slots). Options listed at the slot's exercised 3 credits, in the catalog's printed order. Options in the catalog list at variable credits, disclosed not listed as fixed options: ENGL 200 Independent Study English and Professional Writing (1-4 Hour(s), 3.0 GPA prerequisite), ENGL 221 Special Topics English and Prof Writing (1-4), ENGL 270 Internship in English and Prof Writing (1-4, 3.0 GPA), ENGL 290 Honors Independent Study English and Professional Writing (3-4, 3.5 GPA); the major rule requires each course used toward the major to be taken for 3 or 4 semester hours. The catalog list also contains a plain-text row 'HUMN 105 - Narratives of Health and Healing' that is not a link and has no detail page; no HUMN 105 exists in this catalog (catalog search returns no matches; only ENGL 105/HHMN 105 exist), so it is not listed. ENGL 105 is cross-listed with HHMN 105; ENGL 225 is cross-listed with WGSS 225 (not an option in this list); ENGL 365 is cross-listed with REST 365.
